claims.summary: For alpha_1, alpha_2 in (0,infinity] with 1/alpha_1 + 1/alpha_2 >= 1/2, L_0 the constant of thm:per-level-count-matchings, L > 0, levels 1 <= t_2 <= t_1 <= log N, D_j = L sqrt(log N/N) t_j^(1/alpha_j), H the pairs within D_1 in the first coordinate and G those of H within D_2 in the second, X, Y independent uniform samples of size N in [0,1]^2, and a level t' in [1, log N] with L_0 t'^(1/alpha_j) <= L t_j^(1/alpha_j) for j = 1, 2: with probability tending to one every chain of lem:two-graph-chain-duality for the 0/1 cost of length ell has value at most (ell + 1) 2N e^(-t'), and at most ell 2N e^(-t') if N min(D_1,1) min(D_2,1) >= (1+delta) log N for a fixed delta > 0; so chains of length up to e^(t' - t_2) have value at most 2N e^(-t_2) under that condition. At (4,4), t_1 = log N, t_2 = sqrt(log N), with t' = (1+lambda) t_2 and L >= L_0 (1+lambda)^(1/4), a refutation of the strict both-high mixed counts needs a chain longer than e^(lambda sqrt(log N)).
claims.assessment: Working proof: the per-level matching at level t' lies in G but for 2N e^(-t') pairs, and along its pairs in G the chain's level indices satisfy w >= u; the indices of uncovered vertices differ by at most ell + 1 (no Y-point isolated in H, always with probability tending to one), or ell when no Y-point is isolated in G (each box of area at least min(D_1,1) min(D_2,1) empty with probability at most N^(-(1+delta)), a union over the N points). The first bound is cor:short-chains-per-level's argument with its level free; the isolated-point step gains the factor ell/(ell+1).
claims.rationale: Pushes any refutation of the strict both-high mixed counts to chains longer than e^(t' - t_2), t' the highest level whose box lies in G.
claims.next_action: Bound the length of an optimal chain, through the range of an optimal integral dual potential or a G-matching chosen per level.
